newsitem.title: USA: Groves in good condition in Florida citrus belt.
newsitem.headline: Groves in good condition in Florida citrus belt.

text.p: Florida's citrus groves are in good condition this week, although rain is needed, and many caretakers and growers continue to run low volume irrigation to maintain good tree condition, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS) said.
There is an abundance of new foliage on trees of all ages acccording to FASS.
Most trees have completed blooming and petal drop.
Caretakers are mowing, chopping, and discing cover crops to help save surface moisture. Hedging and topping are going on in all areas, FASS said.
FASS said an estimated 4,677,000 boxes of Valencia oranges were harvested in the week ended March 30, up from 4,019,000 in the prior week and compared with 2,887,000 during the week ended March 16.
An estimated 16,000 boxes of early and mid oranges were harvested in the week ended March 30, down from 207,000 boxes the prior week, FASS said.
